public.title: Expiring Storage
public.description: Operations are ["set",time,key,value,ttl], ["get",time,key], or ["remove",time,key]. Times are nondecreasing integers 0 through 1000; ttl is 0 through 1000. set replaces value and expiry time+ttl. get returns null if absent or current time is at least expiry; otherwise the value. Mutations return null. Supported inputs contain at most 100 array entries per sequence and at most 20 operations or requests per sequence, at most 60 total object properties and array elements in any single JSON value, nesting depth at most 8, strings at most 100 ASCII characters unless specified otherwise, and integers from -100 through 100 unless a tighter or explicit alternate bound is stated. The entire argument JSON encoding is at most 1000 bytes. Nested sequences collectively have at most 100 entries; output snapshots therefore remain bounded. Inputs always satisfy the described shape and bounds.
hints: Expiry is inclusive: a value is gone exactly at its expiry time.
Check the public examples against the documented empty-input and boundary rules.

explanation: Map each key to value and absolute expiry; replacing a key replaces both. Queries compare virtual time without sleeping. O(n) expected time and O(n) space. This JSON adapter verifies observable results; it does not establish built-in-method restrictions, garbage collection, browser behavior or real timer/microtask scheduling.
